To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

glibenclamid, a drug used for treating non-insulin‐dependent diabetes mellitus, opposes the inhibitory action of glucagon and of epinephrin on the key hepatic glycoytic enzymes phosphofractokinase and pyruvated kinase.

the sulphonylurea glibenclamides reduces the inhibitory effect on two key glycolytic hepatic enzymes of glucagon and of epinephrin, which are known to stimulate gluconeogenesis, thus favouring glucose uptake and glycolysis.
glibenclamidemight be a new drug for diabetes mellitus, because of its insulin‐like action on the liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extra‐pancreatic effects of gliben‐ clamide.
the question of whether the antidiabetic action of sulfonylureas is limited to an action at the pancreatic β‐cell or whether they have also extra‐pancreatic actions.
the extra‐pancreatic effects of glibenclaide, which are of interest in the search for a new generation of oral hypoglycemic agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glibenclamid is an insulin‐like compound, which, in contrast to insulin, acts on the key enzymes of glycolysis and gluconeogenesis.
glibenclamid has an insulin‐like effect on liver glucose metabolism.
glibenclamides extra‐pancreatic effects in man, if any, are very small, if they occur at all.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glibenclamides inhibitory action on the pancreatic β‐cell KATP‐channel is the most prominent, but not the only, effect of this drug in man.
glibenclamid, in the presence of insulin, has an additional action on liver metabolism, i.e. it reduces the inhibitory effects of glucagon and/or epinephrine.

glibenclamid is a dual‐acting antidiabetic drug with a pronounced hypoglycemic action and a pronounced hypolipidemic action, and that the hypoglycemia and the hypolipidemia are not only caused by an insulin‐like effect on peripheral tissue, but also by an insulin‐antagonistic effect on pancreatic β‐cell function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glibenclamides effect on the hepatic enzymes is not limited to the pancreatic beta cells but also affects extra-pancreatic organs.
glibenclamides extra‐pancreatic effect on gluconeogenesis may have a role in its therapeutic use.
glibenclamde has a direct, extra-pancreatic effect, reducing the inhibition of key hepatic glycoyltic enzymes by glucagon and epinphrine.
